summary: You have built a sensible, Australia-focused reef-monitoring concept with a clear, feasible week-by-week Gantt plan and a reasonable set of references. The main gaps are stated mission requirements, a link from the concept to space-segment design, a corrected acidification and bleaching explanation, and some technical results. Addressing these would move several criteria up a level.
next_steps: Correct the acidification and bleaching causal chain, and verify or remove the unreferenced claims about the 100 m pixel comparison and the hundreds-of-millions figure.
Write a concise requirements table covering orbit regime, altitude, payload, coverage and latency, and trace each requirement to your mission goals and user needs.
Produce your first STK results, such as orbit parameters or ground-track outputs, with a short interpretation, and add contingency provisions for slipped tasks to your Gantt plan.

criteria.C1: Your purpose of monitoring Great Barrier Reef bleaching and your primary users, marine and conservation scientists, are clear and footnoted. To reach Accomplished, state quantified mission requirements (orbit, altitude, payload, coverage, latency) and link them to space-segment design. Identify further users such as reef managers. Correct the claim that acidification causes bleaching, since thermal stress is the main driver, and reference or remove the unsupported claims.
criteria.C2: Your week-by-week Gantt chart covers all major tasks with dates, status colours and descriptions, and the plan is clearly feasible. Week 10 is reserved for review, which is a good decision. To reach Accomplished, add explicit contingency and variation provisions for slipped or extended tasks, and explain why the sequencing suits the mission narrative. Ensure each information source is cited consistently.
criteria.C3: You have completed a literature review, read the bleaching-monitoring brief and finished STK tutorials 1 to 4. No technical results are yet presented. To reach Accomplished, include a good set of preliminary results, for example STK orbit parameters, coverage or ground-track outputs, each with a brief interpretation showing you are on track for completion.
criteria.C4: Your report has a logical structure with clear headings, and the writing is mostly fluent. The Gantt chart is readable, but it lacks a figure caption and its red deadline lines are hard to see. Footnote citations do not map one-to-one to the Useful Links list, and some wording is informal. To reach Accomplished, caption all figures, improve contrast, align references with the list, and polish the language.
